releases.note:
Three compatibility fixes and a couple of UI improvements.

This release is a collection of some UI improvements, compatibility
enhancements and a bit of work to make content in this repo easy to import and
reuse in the new  https://llama-swap.ai website.

Thanks to everyone who filed detailed bugs and contributed changes. The
quality of this project would not be where it is without the community.

----

- [1249e7c](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/commit/1249e7c8b53b56dcb079a117fe1aa8ab5fa414cb) changelog: make into package: makes `changelog/` an importable Go package with `Versions()`, `Latest()` and `Get()` over the embedded per-release markdown so llama-swap.ai can display the release notes by [@mostlygeek](https://github.com/mostlygeek)
- [PR #1315](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/1315) ui: reduce ActivityTable render rate: throttles the Activity table to one render every 125 ms and skips redraws while the inflight panel is hidden, because live token/duration counters repainted on every update and burned CPU whenever several streams were active by [@mostlygeek](https://github.com/mostlygeek)
- [PR #1318](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/1318) UI: category and a capability badge for decision models: gives models declaring the `decision` capability their own sidebar/list category and a matching badge, since categories were derived from capabilities but decision models fell through with neither by [@sousekd](https://github.com/sousekd)
- [PR #1319](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/1319) internal/server: pass through 1xx interim responses in recorders: forwards 1xx statuses without recording them, because `Expect: 100-continue` (sent by curl for bodies over about 1 MiB) made the recorders latch onto the relayed `100 Continue` and discard the real status, so upstream 400/500 errors arrived at the client as 200 by [@mostlygeek](https://github.com/mostlygeek)
- [PR #1326](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/1326) Remove metadata filtering to allow custom fields alongside capabilities: stops dropping `architecture`, `capabilities`, `supported_parameters`, `context_length` and `context_window` from user `metadata` when capabilities are set, since that metadata is nested under `meta.llamaswap` and cannot collide with the generated top-level fields by [@mostlygeek](https://github.com/mostlygeek)
- [PR #1327](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/1327) Add autoload=false support to /props endpoint: answers `GET /props?autoload=false` with 409 instead of loading a model that is not running (as llama-server's router mode does), so clients like llama.vscode that probe every listed model no longer load them one after another and evict the loaded model by [@mostlygeek](https://github.com/mostlygeek)

ggml-backend : prefetch only inputs computed by earlier splits (#32100)

* ggml-backend : prefetch only inputs computed by earlier splits

The copy callback of a split runs after the prefetch and can write tensors that a later split reads, e.g. the MoE cache uploads missed experts into its bank. A prefetch of such a tensor reads it before the write.

* llama : skip the MoE cache when its device cannot run the cached mul_mat_id

Otherwise the scheduler runs the matmul on another backend and copies the whole bank every ubatch.

CUDA: skip empty MoE tiles in MMQ stream-k fixup (#32067)

* CUDA: skip empty MoE tiles in MMQ stream-k fixup

mul_mat_q_stream_k_fixup loads ids_dst[col_low + j] for all j < J before
checking j_sup. mul_mat_q returns early on col_low == col_high, the fixup
kernel did not. mm_ids_helper emits one extra tile per expert that may be
empty; for trailing experts col_low == ncols_dst, so the load reads one
element past the J_best-1 padding added in #29953. The kernel returns at
j >= j_sup before storing anything, so results are unaffected.

Return early when j_sup <= 0, like the main kernel. The return is
block-uniform (tsj is loaded once per block) and precedes __syncthreads().

Add test_mul_mat_id_unused_tail to test-backend-ops: only the first
n_mats/2 experts are selected, so the trailing experts have zero rows and
their tiles are empty; m=33, k=512 keeps tile efficiency low enough that
stream-k splits along K and launches the fixup kernel.

* server : throttle download progress per file

Files of a download run in parallel threads, but progress updates were
throttled with one shared timer. A small draft sidecar reports far more
often than the main weights, so it took nearly every slot and the main
file's updates, including the first one carrying its total size, were
dropped until the draft finished. The UI then showed the draft's progress
first and restarted from 0% for the model.

Throttle each file on its own and always pass a file's first update.

cuda : use MMVF for BF16 matrices of few rows at small batch sizes (#31959)

MMF tiles 32 rows per block, so a BF16 matrix with few rows (e.g. the
qwen4exp hyper-connection projections, 320 rows with K = 10240) runs only
a handful of blocks and leaves most SMs idle at batch sizes 2..8. MMVF
runs a block per row and wins there when K is long enough.

MMVF's cost grows with rows x batch while MMF's stays roughly flat in that
range, so use MMVF only while rows * ne11 * 256 <= nsm * min(K, max_k) and
K >= 1024. The budget scales with the SM count, which keeps GPUs with few
SMs (e.g. the A16) on MMF. Blackwell allows up to 8 columns and
max_k = 6144; older GPUs stop at 5 columns and max_k = 4096.

Add eval cases at 128x2560, 512x2560 and 320x10240 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8.

vulkan: add tiled-transpose concat shader for Qwen models (#30591)

* vulkan: tiled transpose for dim-0 concat with a transposed source

The delta-net conv-state path does ggml_transpose() straight into a dim-0
ggml_concat(), so the generic concat kernel reads src1 with the transposed
stride, one element per thread, and neighbouring lanes land on different cache
lines. Stage a 32x32 tile through shared memory instead, which keeps both the
load and the store coalesced. 33 columns pads away the bank conflicts.

Gated narrowly: dim 0, 2D, unquantized 4-byte elements, contiguous src0/dst
rows, and src1 actually transposed. Everything else falls through to the
existing kernel.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on gfx1151/RADV, 30 gated-delta-net layers: the CONCAT op goes
11877 us -> 957 us, and pp2048 at ub2048 goes 1224 -> 1628 t/s. Generated text
is unchanged.

The approach follows the tiled transposed concat Gaetan Puleo wrote for the HIP
backend in his Strix Halo fork.

ggml-rpc : fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes (#30415)

* ggml-rpc: fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes

rpc_dispatcher::start() aborted the whole process (GGML_ABORT -> SIGABRT) when
the endpoint could not be parsed, the transport failed to initialise, the socket
could not connect, or the HELLO handshake failed. A typo in --rpc or a
temporarily down node killed the host application, and the reason went to a log
stream the host may never see.

Make the connect-time failure reportable instead of fatal: start() returns bool
(LOG_ERROR + false; the dispatcher thread only starts after a successful
handshake), negotiate_hello() returns false on a half-open socket,
get_dispatcher() returns nullptr and does not cache failed attempts, and every
consumer treats nullptr as "endpoint did not answer" with the conservative
behaviour of its domain (allocation -> nullptr, alloc-size -> lower bound,
device memory -> 0/0, events -> no-op, device count -> 0, and add_server()
already maps 0 devices to nullptr).

Mid-stream failures keep the existing RPC_STATUS_ASSERT by design (fail fast
against silent corruption) and are intentionally out of scope.

Field motivation: on Android (llama.rn + phone RPC cluster) an unreachable
worker crashed the app; the crash buffer showed
abort <- ggml_abort <- rpc_dispatcher::start <- ggml_backend_rpc_add_server.

* tests : add a regression test for unreachable rpc endpoints

Calls ggml_backend_rpc_add_server with a socket that nothing listens on and with a
malformed endpoint, and expects nullptr from both. Without the fix in this branch
the first call aborts the process, so the test cannot even fail cleanly.

* ggml-rpc remove low-value comments

* tests : drop the internal device-count check after the rpc registry refactor

vulkan: cap scalar flash attention at 8 rows for large heads on Qualcomm (#30829)

With head sizes above 128 and KV >= 1024, scalar flash attention uses
16 rows per workgroup. On the Qualcomm Adreno driver this variant
spills registers to scratch memory (264 bytes per invocation on the
X1-85, none at 8 rows) and runs about 40x slower. The largest
test-backend-ops case then becomes a single dispatch of several
seconds, past the Windows GPU timeout, and the test never completes on
the X1 Elite.

Use at most 8 rows per workgroup on Qualcomm when hsk or hsv > 128.
Smaller heads keep 16 rows, which is faster for them on the X2 Elite.

Adreno X1-85, FLASH_ATTN_EXT hsk=256 kv=4096: nb=64 711 ms -> 17 ms,
nb=512 no result -> 125 ms; test-backend-ops completes. Adreno X2-90:
Gemma 4 E4B pp512 at depth 4096 with flash attention 81-90 -> 117 t/s.

server : fix response_format json_schema when schema is not nested in the json_schema wrapper (#28697)

* server : accept top-level schema in response_format with type json_schema

The OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint only applied the schema
when it was nested inside response_format.json_schema.schema. When the
schema was provided directly as response_format.schema (as documented in
the server README, and used by some clients), it was silently ignored
and generation ran unconstrained.

Also mention json_schema in the error message for invalid response_format
types, document the OpenAI wrapper form in the README, and add a test
case for the top-level schema form.

Fixes #10732

* server : let the json_schema wrapper take precedence by presence

Pick the schema source based on whether response_format has a
json_schema key, instead of falling back when the parsed wrapper schema
is empty. An empty schema {} is valid (any JSON value), so the old check
let a top-level schema override an explicit {} in the wrapper. Use
json_value() for the top-level schema too, like the rest of the
function, and add tests for the precedence.

ggml : implement the backward pass for TRI (#30712)

* ggml: implement the backward pass for TRI

GGML_OP_TRI had no case in the backward switch, so a trainable graph containing it aborted with "unsupported ggml op for backward pass: TRI". The op is linear, so its gradient is masked the same way. The incoming gradient is not necessarily contiguous (the backward of a transpose hands over a view) and ggml_tri requires contiguity, so it is made contiguous first.

test_tri gains a post_transpose variant (out = transpose(tri(a))) that aborts as above without this change.

* ggml : simplify the TRI backward pass

Pass the gradient directly to ggml_tri and drop the transpose test. The existing TRI cases cover the backward pass for contiguous F32 gradients.
